chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What attaches to a man after his death?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A Sunnah that he established which is acted upon after his death, so there will be for him a reward like that of the one who acts by it, without any deficiency in their rewards; and flowing charity which flows after him; and a righteous child who supplicates for his parents after their death, and performs Hajj on their behalf, and gives charity on their behalf, and emancipates (a slave), and fasts, and prays on their behalf.' I said: 'Shall I share them in my Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.

key_terms.أُشْرِكُهُمَا: To share them (the parents) in the reward of my action.
key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ الْجَارِيَةُ: Continuous charity, where the reward persists as long as the charity is used.
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ الصَّالِحُ: A righteous child who performs good deeds and supplications for their parents.
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: A practice or tradition established by the deceased that others continue to follow.

ai.seo_question: What deeds continue to benefit a person after their death according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Kafi establishes the concept of 'Amal al-Mutawassi' (continuing deeds), emphasizing that the reward for the deceased remains undiminished while the living retain their own full share. It specifically validates the Shia practice of performing Hajj, fasting, and prayer on behalf of the deceased, as confirmed by Imam al-Sadiq's affirmation to Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar. This narration serves as a primary textual basis for the permissibility of vicarious worship in Shia jurisprudence.
